name: Colonial Crawl
description:
In this walk, we will explore how the British sahibs, memsahibs, and royalty left their mark on the garden city.What makes this tour specialWe will start at Cubbon Park, soaking in the freshness in the avenue of trees. Inside the park, we will explore parts that house statues, offices of importance, and landmarks that put Bangalore on the world map. Not to forget, the role of Mark Cubbon in shaping the city, and why the park was named after him.

Once we’re done with this, we will visit a secret garden as well as stroll along St. Mark’s Road to discover Winston Churchill’s life in the area, and end it with breakfast at an iconic eatery.

Bangalore mornings are arguably the best, and we promise to make the walk a memorable one for you with all the area has to offer. All you have to do is join us on the crawl.You can add your images, videos and itinerary route in lightbox for each itinerary as shown below, simply by changing the src path of each media.The Colonial Crawl is a taste of history hidden right under your noses. In this walk, we will explore how the British sahibs, memsahibs, and royalty left their mark on the garden city.

The English influence on the sprawling Cubbon park, the origins of the Cantonment area, and the surrounding architecture are testimony to a lot of events in history. For example, the American War of Independence, the Battle of Waterloo, and the French Revolution had a connection to this region. We will spill more of this tea when you walk with us.
 Whether you are visiting or you are a local, we promise you will see the city in a different light once you learn about the colonial influence on its churches, clubs, parks, and its people.

Cubbon mornings are a sight to sore eyes, and the perfect time to discover the Colonial Hangover in one of the older parts of the city.

name: Malleshwaram Hogona
description:
This street art walk featuring 13 Indian artists and 12 artworks is an initiative by the Bengaluru Moving Campaign in association with the artist collective Geechugalu and several other partners to make the neighbourhood of Malleshwaram safe and friendly for women mobility. Gully Tours was the official partner to design the walking tour.What makes this tour specialWe’ll start this walk by relishing some legendary dosa at Shri Sagar CTR. From there we’ll visit the conservancy lanes that are adorned with art. We’ll explore the Malleshwaram market, seva sadan, sampige road, and end it at the BMTC bus stand.

Malleswaram is like a warm hug from a handmade shawl on a cold winter day. It’s a modern-day Malgudi with the goodness of history and the excitement of new-age quirks.

Street art captures the stories of people, their lives, and their neighbourhoods. Show some love to your local artists and let us go to Malleswaram.You can add your images, videos and itinerary route in lightbox for each itinerary as shown below, simply by changing the src path of each media.13 Indian artists came together to create 12 walls filled with art through the secret lanes of Malleswaram to reclaim spaces for pedestrians and women. The Malleswaram Hogona (Eng: Let’s go to Malleswaram) street art project wants to make streets safer for women. Conceived by the Bengaluru moving project, this street art walk is an initiative to make neighbourhoods safe, friendly, and full of character.

Apart from being one of the oldest planned neighbourhoods in the city, it houses a flower market, many institutions and lanes adorned with trees. Each work of art tells you the artist’s inspiration and their connection to the landscape, and we’d love to host you here.

Let’s go to Malleswaram to witness modern day murals painted on old world lanes, starting with a legendary breakfast at CTR.

name: The Soba Walk
description:
On the SoBa Walk, we’ll witness the co-existence of the old and new weaved together by the various communities, heritage structures, and houses.What makes this tour specialWe will start closer to the National College Metro station, soaking in the freshness offered by the avenue of trees. From there, we’ll venture into different streets and explore old houses in the neighbourhood. We will also visit a bazaar that has everything under the sun, and go to temples that have stood the test of time and have tales to awe entire generations.

We’ll end the trail with a delicious South Indian breakfast that is nutritious, tasty, and one of Bangalore’s best fares in town.

This is a walk for anyone who loves to explore the  modern, simple yet rich side of South BangaloreYou can add your images, videos and itinerary route in lightbox for each itinerary as shown below, simply by changing the src path of each media.Manhattan has SoHo, Mumbai has SoBo, and namma Bengaluru has SoBa - South Bangalore. The land of playwrights, artists, and authors, Basavanagudi can be dubbed as the cultural capital of Bangalore (no offence to Malleswaram and North Bangalore peeps). In fact, most roads in this part of the city are named in the honour of these creative legends.

On the SoBa Walk, we’ll witness the co-existence of the old and new weaved together by the various communities, heritage structures, and houses. We will walk through the bazaar and its specialities, visit a centuries old temple, and learn how this part of Bangalore has managed to retain its old-world charm.

Join us as we explore one of the oldest neighbourhoods of Bangalore, the intellectual nerve centre of the city and get to know where the rich and the famous hung out.

name: The Tiffin Trail
description:
This trail is an ode to the tiffin culture of Bangalore and trying out food at all the iconic eateries in Bangalore of the 60s and 70s.What makes this tour specialWe will start at Vidyarthi Bhavan, the OG Bangalore eatery, with dose in typical Bangalorean style. We’ll then venture into different streets and explore old houses in the neighbourhood, visit hotels and cafes that are always ready to serve hot fare in windy, cold evenings of Bangalore.

We will discover why the menu at these places hasn’t changed in decades, what are some of their best-selling dishes, and uncover some of the lesser-known secrets of the city’s history

This is a walk for anyone who loves to explore the sleepy, yet vibrant side of Bangalore.You can add your images, videos and itinerary route in lightbox for each itinerary as shown below, simply by changing the src path of each media.The trend of tiffins is unique to Bangalore. A local snack soiree that began in the bylanes of Basavanagudi is now quintessential to the Bangalore lifestyle.

In the tiffin trail, we explore how this story began, people who brought in the tiffin concept and what makes these eateries so special. This South Bangalore trail also takes you on a nostalgia tour of Bangalore in the 60s and 70s, which was the land of playwrights, artists, and authors.

The eateries where these greats hung out still exist and serve their humble fare to crowds even today, some of whom still serve the same dishes since their inception. But this trail is not just about food. It lets you explore and understand what city planning, local bazaars, and vintage charms feels like.

name: Cantt by Night
description:
This walk is about different communities that built modern Bangalore. Before the bazaars became popular, Cantonment saw activists, entrepreneurs, and social reformers in the erstwhile British India.What makes this tour specialWe will start the tour at a heritage bungalow and wade through the residential lanes of Shivajinagar, ending it closer to Commercial Street.

We will explore 100 year old structures, visit different small businesses, and learn about the various historical figures that contributed to education, jobs, and opportunities for the people as well as savour the local favourite snacks and food that are distinct to this part of the city.

This walk has been specially curated by a local resident, who grew up in the Commercial Street neighbourhood and has lived its rich history.You can add your images, videos and itinerary route in lightbox for each itinerary as shown below, simply by changing the src path of each media.Bangalore’s Cantonment areas are extra special. It’s a melting pot of cultures built together by the locals, immigrants, and the British. In Cantt by night, we will be exploring the lesser-known side of Commercial street, which goes beyond the regular street shopping fare. There are houses, shops, institutions and more that carry the legacy of leaders and prominent names in Bangalore’s history. And of course, no legacy is complete without the presence of food. From a family-run dosa joint to a 48-year-old sweet shop and a legacy bakery, there’s a brilliant food mix on the menu as you explore the ruins and reigns of one of Bangalore’s most popular shopping districts.
